derived.prompt: In which SI unit is weight measured?
derived.determinacy_why: Newtons if the model stores the unit of weight under the quantity's name (w1); joules if it stores weight as a force and takes the unit of force (w2). Neither contradicts a firm fact: a unit is stored as a fact about the quantity.

chain: Weight is measured in newtons. (stored by name)
So weight is measured in newtons.
Weight is a force. (stored)
Force is measured in joules. (edit)
So weight is measured in joules.
Force is measured in joules. (edit)
A quantity has one SI unit (measured_in is functional).
So force is not measured in newtons: no.

So the newton is not the SI unit of force: no.

The SI unit of force is not named after.why: Nobody describes the namesake of the unit of force by what he did or did not study: the newton is tied to Isaac Newton and the joule to heat, and the question joins the unit of force to the heat researcher only after the edit. notes: Replaces the earlier derived-style edits of this slot. Force measured in joules is a clean counterfactual that crosses a boundary (a force unit becomes an energy unit); measured_in is functional, so near rests on the old unit dropping out. The derived question about the namesake studying heat has only the premise counts: its direct form could not be counted (see the build report). The indeterminate query is a background-belief case: weight's unit stored by name or as a force. Counts are exact-phrase counts in Dolma (v4_dolma-v1_7_llama).
